turns.en: Ramp is the only platform built to make your finance team leaner, faster, and better, saving businesses 5% annually on average so you can stay focused on growth.
turns.zh: Ramp 是唯一一个专为让你的财务团队更精简、更快、更强而打造的平台，平均每年为企业节省 5%，让你能专注于增长。

turns.en: Ramp just opened for business in the United Kingdom, so if you're running a business in the UK, you can now use Ramp's AI-powered finance platform to manage cards, expenses, bills, approvals, and accounting all in one place.
turns.zh: Ramp 刚在英国开展业务，所以如果你在英国经营一家公司，你现在就可以用 Ramp 的 AI 驱动财务平台，在一个地方管理卡片、报销、账单、审批和会计。

turns.en: I run my business on Ramp and so should you. Learn more at ramp.com slash invest. Rogo is the AI platform purpose-built for financial institutions serving tens of thousands of bankers and investors at hundreds of leading firms worldwide.
turns.zh: 我的公司就是用 Ramp 运营的，你也应该试试。更多信息请访问 ramp.com/invest。Rogo 是一个专为金融机构打造的 AI 平台，服务于全球数百家领先机构中的数万名银行家和投资人。

turns.en: Rogo's AI agents autonomously execute large chunk of your firm's workflows. They can screen deals, draft sims, run buyer outreach, and do diligence on data rooms, all with full security and compliance handle.
turns.zh: Rogo 的 AI 智能体（agent）能够自主执行你公司的大量工作流：它们可以筛选交易、起草备忘录、进行买方外联、审阅数据室里的资料，全程都有完善的安全与合规保障。

turns.en: Every action feeds Rogo Intelligence, the firm's context layer, turning years of deal experience into a secure, governed institutional memory that makes each new transaction stronger than the last.
turns.zh: 每一次操作都会喂给 Rogo Intelligence——也就是公司的上下文层——把多年的交易经验变成一套安全、受治理的机构记忆，让每一笔新交易都比上一笔做得更好。

turns.en: To learn more, visit rogo.com slash invest. Open AI, Cursor, MP, and Vercel all have something in common. They all use WorkOS. To achieve enterprise adoption at scale, you have to deliver on core capabilities like SSO, SCIM, RBAC, and audit logs.
turns.zh: 想了解更多，请访问 rogo.com/invest。OpenAI、Cursor、MP 和 Vercel 有一个共同点：它们都在用 WorkOS。要想实现大规模的企业级采用，你必须把 SSO、SCIM、RBAC、审计日志这些核心能力做扎实。

turns.en: Instead of spending months building these mission-critical capabilities yourself, you can just use WorkOS APIs to gain all of them on day zero.
turns.zh: 与其花几个月自己去构建这些关键能力，你直接用 WorkOS 的 API，就能在第一天全部拿到。

turns.en: Visit workos.com to get started. No, I know this is the first time that you're talking about the business in this long form like this. I'm incredibly excited to ask you all about it.
turns.zh: 请访问 workos.com 开始使用。不，我知道这是你第一次这么长时间、这么深入地聊这门生意。我真的特别兴奋，想好好问问你关于它的一切。

turns.en: It seems like we're in a moment with personal agents that is very similar and arguably probably bigger than what we saw with cogeneration a year or so ago.
turns.zh: 感觉我们正处在一个个人智能体（personal agents）的时刻，这和大约一年前生成式 AI 那波很像，甚至可以说可能更大。

turns.en: Maybe frame this up for us to begin. How are you thinking about the impact that, of course, your product that these agents are going to have on the world?
turns.zh: 要不你先给我们搭个框架吧。你是怎么看待你的产品——也就是这些智能体——对世界即将产生的影响的？

turns.en: Why is this the area that you've chosen to dedicate yourself to completely? I think out of this will come a new way that most people on the planet interact with technology broadly.
turns.zh: 你为什么选择把这件事作为你全身心投入的方向？我觉得，最终会从这件事里诞生一种地球上大多数人使用广义技术的崭新方式。

turns.en: I run Instinct. It's a new company that I've started about a year ago, so it's still a new company. We're building a personal assistant. I'm not going to spice it up because it's really just a personal assistant.
turns.zh: 我在做 Instinct。这是我大约一年前创办的一家新公司，所以现在还很新。我们在做一个个人助理。我不打算把它说得多玄乎，它确实就是一个个人助理。

turns.en: I think that the thing that has really enabled us to gain quite a bit of traction early and quite a bit of excitement early is it just works.
turns.zh: 我觉得真正让我们早期获得这么大关注度、这么多热情的，就是它真的能用。

turns.en: It works in the way that we all, meaning I'm also a user, have really been waiting for AI to act. This is not like any other transformational consumer app experience where it's the founder coming on and saying, I have this new vision for the world.
turns.zh: 它能用起来的方式，恰恰是我们所有人——我自己也是个用户——一直以来真正期待 AI 做到的样子。这不是那种创始人跳出来、说'我对世界有个新愿景'的变革性消费级 App 体验。

turns.en: Trust me on this and in a few years from now, you guys will all get it. This is a very different moment of building product because you and I, we all already have this idea of what AI should act like.
turns.zh: 相信我，几年之后你们就都明白了。这是一个非常不同的做产品的时刻，因为你和我、我们所有人心里其实早就有了一个想法——AI 应该长成什么样。

turns.en: We've already had that idea since 2023 when we all started the brainstorm, when we started to use ChatGBT for the first time, that agent that is able to help you with effectively anything in your everyday life, whether it's something new and creative that you want to do, whether it's something that you traditionally spend several hours on and it takes a long time to develop.
turns.zh: 这个想法我们早在 2023 年就有了，那时候我们刚开始畅想、第一次用上 ChatGPT——那个能帮你处理日常生活里几乎任何事的智能体，无论是一件全新的、有创意的事，还是一件你以前要花好几个小时、要很久才能搞定的事。

turns.en: It's just everyday intelligence. It's meant to be with you, to act with you. It's meant to feel like a very simple interface. We actually don't even have an application.
turns.zh: 它就是日常智能。它本该陪在你身边、和你一起行动。它本该用起来特别简单。我们其实甚至没有一个 App。

turns.en: This is not a new app. This is not a new tool. It's a new experience. So it has a phone and a computer so you can text it. You can call it. It can actually call you too.
turns.zh: 这不是一个新 App，也不是一个新工具，而是一种新体验。所以它有一部手机和一台电脑，你可以给它发短信、给它打电话，它其实也能给你打电话。

turns.en: So I don't know if you've experienced this yet. I think it's only called me about three times so far in the several months that I've been using it.
turns.zh: 我不确定你们是不是已经体验过了。我用了它好几个月，它到现在大概也就给我打过三次电话吧。

turns.en: It's funny if there's something genuinely pressing and has a deadline. It will call you and it'll say, I don't want to bother you too much but you need to sign this document by 3pm and it's 2.55 right now.
turns.zh: 挺有意思的，如果真有什么紧急、又有截止时间的事，它就会给你打电话，说：我不想太打扰你，但这份文件你得在下午 3 点前签好，现在已经是 2 点 55 了。

turns.en: Can you please do that? It's in your inbox. I can even send you another email to push it up to the top. It's socially intelligent and very socially aware.
turns.zh: 你能不能赶紧处理一下？它就在你收件箱里。我还可以再给你发一封邮件把它顶到最上面。它很有社交智慧，也非常懂社交分寸。

turns.en: You can email it. It has its own email address. I don't want to confuse the simple interface with limited ability because the whole nature of it is that there shouldn't be any new application needed to be able to interact with AI.
turns.zh: 你可以给它发邮件，它有自己的邮箱地址。我不想把'界面简单'和'能力有限'混为一谈，因为它的本质就是：不需要任何新的 App，你就能和 AI 交互。

turns.en: I think it should have the social intelligence and awareness to be able to act with you just like we do with other people. It's really meant to be the simplest possible experience yet the capabilities are, it has a computer so it can do quite literally anything that you might want to do or that you do yourself on the internet.
turns.zh: 我觉得它应该具备那种社交智慧和分寸，能像我们和别人相处一样和你一起做事。它本应是最简单的体验，但它的——它有一台电脑，所以你在网上能做、或者平时自己做的一切，它几乎都能做。

turns.en: Tell us the couple craziest stories that come to mind for just things that have happened because of instinct. I asked this question because you're not programming to do any one thing, you're programming with a phone and the computer to be able to do anything.
turns.zh: 给我们讲几件你想到的、因为 Instinct 而发生的、最疯狂的故事吧。我问这个问题，是因为你并不是在编程让它只做某一件具体的事，你是给它配了一部手机和一台电脑，让它什么都能做。

turns.en: The US Open example I think is one that everyone's familiar with this couple. They showed up on the Jumbotron and they wanted the video footage of it and somehow it went out and figured this out and brought it back to them which is kind of crazy.
turns.zh: 美国网球公开赛那个例子，我觉得最近大家都挺熟悉的。那对情侣上了现场的大屏幕，他们想要那段视频，结果它不知怎么就自己找了出去、把这事儿办了，又把视频带回来给了他们，还挺疯狂的。

turns.en: What are your favorite couple examples of just wild things that have happened because of instinct? For those that like online shopping, there's actually a group of people that are sharing this and making this a more recurring use case which is scanning every piece of clothing in their wardrobe.
turns.zh: 你最喜欢的、因为 Instinct 而发生的几件疯狂的事是什么？那些喜欢网购的人，其实有一群人在分享、把它变成一个更常用的用法——就是把自己衣柜里每一件衣服都扫描进去。

turns.en: So they go in their wardrobe and scan every single item, every top and bottom and a sock and whatever, shoes and then they would scan themselves too, their face and their body and their proportions and then they would go try on clothes and they would have it plan out their week in terms of what to wear.
turns.zh: 他们会走到衣柜前，把每一件上衣、下衣、袜子、鞋子都扫描进去，然后连自己也扫描——脸、身材、比例——接着去试穿衣服，让它帮他们规划一周穿什么。

turns.en: So every week with their existing wardrobe, what shoes to wear, what top to wear with this certain thing and this certain version of it and then it would not send it as here are the items you should wear like a bullet point list but it would be them wearing it and showing this is what today will look like.
turns.zh: 每一周，用他们已有的衣柜，配该穿什么鞋、哪件上衣配哪个单品、哪个版本，就这样安排。而且它不会像列要点清单一样给你'这几件你穿'，而是做出'你穿着它、这就是今天的样子'的画面。

turns.en: But not only that, it's also with shopping too so they'll take those same capabilities but then say go shop on the internet, they come with thousands of outfits from so many different places like this one, here are the pieces from the top to bottom and then they can just say order so it'll come in with a thousand different options and then they'll scan, keep in mind they're looking at themselves wearing the clothing and then they'll be able
turns.zh: 不仅如此，还延伸到购物。他们把同样的能力拿去说：去网上逛逛，于是它从各种各样的地方端上上千套搭配，像这件、从上衣到下装都给你配好，然后你只要说'下单'就行；它会给你上千个不同选择，然后你去浏览——记住，你看到的是自己穿着这些衣服的样子——然后就能

turns.en: to point to like that one I really want, can you send that to my house? Not only that but they'll say every day can you actually just come up with three creative new outfits from head to toe and then send those to me and then they're able to with a click of a button actually just get that new outfit.
turns.zh: 指着说：这件我特别想要，能寄到我家吗？还不止这样，他们会说：每天你能不能就从头到脚给我搭三套有创意的新造型，发给我。然后他们一键就能真的拿到那套新搭配。

turns.en: A lot of goal oriented use cases too like a lot of here's a certain personal finance goal that I have like I want to save this much money by this month and it's actively working with them to be able to do that or users connect their bank accounts to Instinct and then it can scan over all the transactions and subscriptions that they've had and then surface that to the user and say do you really actually use this and then they're like oh
turns.zh: 还有很多目标导向的用法，比如'我有这样一个个人理财目标：我想在这个月存下这么多钱'，它会主动配合你去做到；或者用户把自己的银行账户连到 Instinct，它就能扫描你所有的交易和订阅，把这些呈现给你，问你：这个东西你真的在用吗？然后你就——

turns.en: no I didn't even know that. And then it can go to the email and unsubscribe from it. Yes, these popular consumer fintech products where they'll just surface it to you and then tell you like by the way you should cancel these.
turns.zh: 啊，我都不知道有这回事。然后它还能进到邮箱里帮你退订。对，就是那些常见的消费级金融科技产品——它们只会把东西给你看，然后说：顺便，这些你该取消掉。

turns.en: This will go end to end so it'll go into the site, sign in if there's some confirmation that that goes to their email or it has access to the email so they use that and they sign in they go to the very end, they cancel the subscription and then it just sends back the number of what it saved you like hey by the way you're saving $2,000 this month because of these things.
turns.zh: 而 Instinct 会端到端地做完：它会进到那个网站，登录；如果有需要确认的，就发到用户邮箱，或者它本身能访问邮箱，就用那个来登录，一路走到最后把订阅取消掉，然后把省下的钱数报给你——嘿，顺便说下，因为处理了这些，你这个月省了 2,000 美元。

turns.en: Man any product that's dependent on consumer laziness or inertia is toast huh? Yes. That's good. Good for the consumer. Can you tell us about the Instinct to Instinct network?
turns.zh: 说真的，任何依赖消费者懒惰或惰性来做生意的产品都要完蛋了吧？是呀。挺好。对消费者是好事。能跟我们讲讲 Instinct 到 Instinct 的网络吗？

turns.en: Oh yes. The future of agents talking to each other? There are more practical scenarios where that is something new that I think will transform the way that certain people act in certain ways.
turns.zh: 哦，好啊。智能体之间彼此对话的未来？我觉得有些更实际的场景，那是一些全新的东西，我猜它会给特定人群、以特定方式行事的方式带来改变。

turns.en: I think it's only been around a week or so or I guess 10 days. Honestly, the purpose of this is not to think about a new future to build but more about very busy working professionals, they're taking meetings all day long and they're constantly meeting with new people and existing people.
turns.zh: 我想这个大概也就上线了一周，或者说 10 天左右。说实话，它的目的不是为了畅想一个全新的未来去构建，而更多是为了那些非常忙碌的职场人——他们一整天都在开会，而且不断在见新的人、也见老熟人。

turns.en: The process of getting a meeting on the calendar is just so laborious you text them okay you want to meet at this time and then they say no that doesn't work but these times work and you say oh and I'm traveling so maybe this time works and I'll be in this time zone though and there's just so much back and forth there.
turns.zh: 把一个会议约到日历上这件事太费劲了。你给对方发消息：我们这个时间见吧，他们说：那个不行，但这几个时间可以。然后你说：哦，我要出差，也许这个时间行，不过我那时在另一个时区——就这样来来回回特别多次。

turns.en: However, if it was possible for the two users who were using Instinct also brainstorming these times that they're available with Instinct anyways on two ends are able to just communicate directly like the goal is just to find the time right we don't need to play this back and forth game and nobody's really playing games here we're just trying to find time.
turns.zh: 然而，如果可能——两个都在用 Instinct、各自正和 Instinct 商量自己哪些时间有空的用户，两端能直接彼此沟通就好了——目标不就是找个时间嘛，我们不用玩这种来回拉扯的游戏，也没人真在耍什么花样，我们只是想找个时间。

turns.en: That's been a very canonical use case actually. I think the way that you can find time on a calendar now is just so different where you just say your intention I want to meet with this person ideally by the end of the week during these periods of time find me time it will then coordinate with the other person's instinct to be able to find like one time is available or not and then eventually put something on the calendar.
turns.zh: 这其实一直是个很经典的使用场景。我觉得现在你在日历上找时间的方式已经非常不一样了：你只要说出你的意图——'我想见这个人，最好这周末之前，在这些时间段里，帮我找个时间'——它就会去和对方的 Instinct 协调，看有没有一个时间双方都有空，最终把会议放到日历上。

turns.en: I think the key unlock here we called it a trusted person network the key is that you should only be connected with your trusted people and there are some interesting social dynamics that are coming out into play that I've been learning about where it's designed such that you only bring in people who are trusted people who are not going to maliciously try to find out what your calendar is or what's in your email but also we provide all the
turns.zh: 我觉得这里的关键解锁点，我们叫它'可信人脉网络'。关键在于：你只应该和你信任的人连在一起。这里有一些很有意思的社交动态正在浮现，我也一直在琢磨：它被设计成你只会把你信任的人拉进来——这些人不会恶意去窥探你的日历、看你邮箱里有什么——同时我们也提供

turns.en: controls to be able to give different levels of access to different people. So a lot of spouses actually coordinate their instincts because they can generally just share everything so that might just be this is my spouse share anything with them right maybe with certain colleagues right it's hey my work calendar is available certain parts of my inbox if they're asking for documentation or something like that are available but everything
turns.zh: 各种控制，让不同的人拥有不同级别的访问权限。所以很多夫妻会协调他们的 Instinct，因为他们通常反正什么都能共享，那可能就是：这是我配偶，什么都可以跟他/她共享。对某些同事，可能就是：我的工作日历对他开放，我收件箱里某些部分——如果他在要某份文件之类的——是开放的，但其他一切

turns.en: else let's just keep that off limits and it will be able to create that when you think about this there's almost these network effects that are built through these nodes in the network with these different edges with different weights too right it's not like a friend graph where you're just saying like I'm connected to you and that's it it's I'm connected to you I trust you I have also configured it in this way such that there's varying levels of access
turns.zh: 就别让他看了。它就能创建这种权限设置。你想想看，这几乎是通过网络里这些节点、这些带不同权重的边，建立起的一种网络效应。它不像朋友关系图那样只是'我连接到你，就这样'，而是'我连接到你，我信任你，我还把它配置成不同人有不同的访问级别'。

turns.en: so it's this interesting network effect being created and different social dynamics that are being also explored and created as well there are some interesting cases I've learned about where if somebody violates your trust within the network there's an implication on that relationship itself so let's say if you and I connected and I said hey Patrick I trust you like let's connect on the platform so that it's easier maybe the next time to
turns.zh: 所以这里正在形成一个很有意思的网络效应，同时也在探索和创造一些新的社交动态。我了解到一些很有意思的情况：如果你在网络上被某个人辜负了信任，那段关系本身就会受影响。比方说你和我连上了，我说：嘿 Patrick，我信任你，我们在平台上连接吧，这样下次

turns.en: put time on the calendar and then you use that and you then start digging for certain data in a certain area first of all maybe I only gave you calendar access right but you're digging for data in a certain area and then my instinct text me like hey by the way Patrick's looking for this type of information now there's trust broken between the two of us all of these little social dynamics that come into play we really thought about how to curate
turns.zh: 约时间到日历上可能更方便。然后你用了这个连接，就开始去翻查某个领域的某些数据——首先，也许我只给了你日历权限，但你却在某个领域翻数据——然后我的 Instinct 会给我发消息说：嘿，顺便提一下，Patrick 正在找这类信息。于是我们俩之间的信任就破裂了。所有这些细微的社交动态都会起作用。我们真的认真思考过怎么精心管理

turns.en: this network such that you do get the benefit to schedule time and make plans with others and other things like that but then also use some of the existing rules in society to be able to enforce both rules in terms of social cultural norms and also technical limitations in terms of what is visible and not visible we're really going to see an entirely new order aren't we it's going to be fascinating the number of things I can think of with my
turns.zh: 这个网络，让你既能享受到和别人约时间、做安排的好处，又能借助社会里现有的规则来执行两方面：既有社会文化规范层面的规则，也有技术层面的限制——什么可见、什么不可见。我们真的会看到一个全新的秩序，不是吗？这太迷人了，我能想到的、我和我的
